常自教兒

review.explanation: The mention 安石 is Xie An's courtesy name (字). The alias registry evidence explicitly identifies 安石 as the courtesy name of 謝安. The main text has Emperor Jianwen (簡文) saying '安石必出' (Anshi will surely come out), which matches the biographical context of Xie An being in seclusion at East Mountain. The candidate evidence from aliases.json directly links 安石 to 謝安. The main text context (謝公在東山畜妓) confirms this is Xie An's story. No contradicting evidence found.

The mention 安 is the abbreviated single-character personal name of 謝安. The Liu annotation from 宋明帝文章志 explicitly states '安縱心事外踈' (An, being carefree and detached), referring to Xie An in the context of the same story about keeping courtesans at East Mountain. The candidate evidence directly asserts identity with 謝安. The annotation is part of the same story (07-shijian-021) and discusses the same person as the main text. No contradicting evidence found.

The mention 謝公 is an honorific office-title reference to Xie An. The alias registry evidence shows 謝公 used in a context about 謝公夫人教兒 (Xie Gong's wife teaching their children), which is consistent with Xie An's family context. The main text begins with 謝公在東山畜妓 (Xie Gong kept courtesans at East Mountain), and Emperor Jianwen's remark about 安石 (Xie An's courtesy name) follows, confirming 謝公 and 安石 refer to the same person. The story is about Xie An's seclusion and eventual emergence. No contradicting evidence found.
